body: Are zoomed items supposed to look like that? From quick testing, some missing features compared to TileSet editor: - The MeshLibrary editor does not automatically appear when selecting a GridMap. You need to unfold the resource. - This is tricky to implement however. You could try to copy the tile editor's solution, but you can also just ignore this feature. - The properties don't show descriptions on hover. - See `add_custom_property_description()`. Not a deal breaker, but using custom inspector makes this easier to add. Also, this a problem with GridMap, but editing any property is super laggy on a scene with GridMap. Tested in 3D platformer demo.

I think it is possible to add vertical layout as well (changing `toolbar` to `FlowContainer` and `item_split` to `SplitContainer`).
Also it looks like 70 is insufficient minimum width for `EditorInspector'. At the same time, the minimum width of `ItemList` could most likely be reduced.

@KoBeWi

> Are zoomed items supposed to look like that?

Nope, fixed.

> - The MeshLibrary editor does not automatically appear when selecting a GridMap. You need to unfold the resource.
> - The properties don't show descriptions on hover. 

Features added.

> Also, this a problem with GridMap, but editing any property is super laggy on a scene with GridMap. Tested in 3D platformer demo.

I guess it depends on the map, since I've been testing with [this repository](https://github.com/Nodragem/top-down-action-adventure-starter-kit) and the changes are instantaneous. Not sure what I can do here.

@arkology

> I think it is possible to add vertical layout as well.

I don't really think it's worthy. A vertical layout would be too cramped to be useful.

> Also it looks like 70 is insufficient minimum width for `EditorInspector`.

Sure, I can increase it a little.

> At the same time, the minimum width of `ItemList` could most likely be reduced.

Seems small enough as is.

> keep the meshes external (seems to not work for some reason)

There seems to be an issue with saving the mesh library after editing with the new editor. Pressing ctrl+s will sometimes not save it, but saving from the inspector button works as expected.

And if I used some code to fetch the Item index, it's not coherent with what the list is showing. (Using a custom resource here) As you can see, Item 13 is showing up at the 16th position in the editor Also, if I switch to a MeshLibrary that only has one item, I can't get the right panel to update:

I believe so

**Import Dock material settings are not reliably applied to selected scenes**

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/120382#issue-4687296976 

There's a good chance it may have snuck under the radar since you weren't prompted to reimport any files when upgrading.

Larger projects often use their own importer scripts while smaller ones tend to just make inherits, but for those with slightly more mature projects relying on this base feature, it's reliability is completely broken

I do wonder what the cause could be though
I was able to reproduce the issue in the 4.7-dev2 version, which doesn't contain this commit. So no, this isn't the cause.
